title: Review of the hunting-ecology dt/2 finding: on fresh seeds 4 and 6 the world's own step halved (0.2 -> 0.1) gives the same counts (predator persistent splits 3 vs 3 and 5 vs 6, generation 1; prey 0 vs 0; mean prey 8.3/9.3 and predators 15.6/8.5 in both)
summary: labkit, 128^2, t=12000, --lineage-k 5 as in the finding: the claim's world at dt 0.2 and the finding's world.py (dt 0.1, 1000 steps per frame) on seeds 4 and 6. Seed 4: prey mean 8.3 / max 19 in both, 0 persistent prey splits in both; predators mean 15.6 in both, max 25 vs 26, persistent splits 3 vs 3, generation 1, merges 1 vs 1. Seed 6: prey mean 9.3 / max 21 in both, 0 vs 0; predators mean 8.5, max 15 in both, persistent splits 5 vs 6, generation 1. The dt/2 sheet shows the same sequence (prey emulsion, predators sweep it at t~2100-3600, prey regrow, second predator wave).

observations.D: predator persistent splits at dt 0.2 vs dt 0.1: 3 vs 3 (seed 4), 5 vs 6 (seed 6), generation 1 in all four runs; prey 0 persistent splits in all four (base/seed4/FACTS.md, dthalf/FACTS.md)

controls_run.D: base/ (claim's world, dt 0.2, seeds 4 and 6) against dthalf/ and dthalf6/ (dt 0.1)

verdicts.limitation: The step test passes, but what it confirms is small: at 128^2 the predators reach only generation 1 and the prey never divide persistently on either seed, so this checks the numerics of the hunting cycle, not D at the claim's 256^2 depth. I did not re-run the g screen.
